speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower what are the projected retrenchment numbers for this year and how does this compare with that of 2015.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how does the Ministry address occurrences of "disguised retrenchments" by employers to avoid paying retrenchment benefits; (b) what measures will the Ministry put in place to monitor and deter such practices; and (c) how will the Government continue to ensure that public sector agencies abide by human resource best practices and do not engage in "disguised retrenchments".

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There is no clear evidence that irresponsible retrenchment is on the rise.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Under the Employment Act, an employee who has served less than two years is not entitled to retrenchment benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those who have served more than two years, payment of retrenchment benefits is mandatory if it is specified in their individual employment contracts or in the collective agreements negotiated by their unions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The prevailing norm at that time was two weeks to one month of salary for each year of service.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are now conducting another survey and the findings will be ready by end of the year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Workers who feel that they have been treated unfairly during any retrenchment exercise can report to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) for investigation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In 2015, MOM received 94 cases from employees with retrenchment-related issues, out of which 15 appeals were from employees who were dismissed but felt they were retrenched and thereby deprived of retrenchment benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the first three quarters of this year, out of 63 retrenchment-related cases, the number of appeals is 14.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, on the whole, these cases account for a small proportion of the total number of local employees retrenched in 2015 and 2016 so far.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In 28 out of these 29 appeals – 15 in 2015 and 14 in 2016 so far – the workers were either not entitled to retrenchment benefits as they have less than two years of service or there were no retrenchment benefits specified in their contracts or collective agreements.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the one remaining appeal, MOM is helping the workers to resolve the issues.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The public sector is committed to progressive human resource practices.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Public sector agencies have signed the Employers' Pledge of Fair Employment Practices since 2007.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They will continue to abide by tripartite guidelines to carry out restructuring responsibly and in consultation with public sector unions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are aware of the different positions of the unions and employers on this, but MOM believes that we can find a way forward for the interests of the retrenched workers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I would just like to seek a few clarifications.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, based on the first three quarters, we already see an almost 33% increase in retrenchment numbers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Based on this rate, I think we can expect for the last quarter, probably over 2,000 more retrenchments.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, my first supplementary question is: is the rate of retrenchment on the increase?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What steps should we take going forward and, in anticipation of the worsening economic climate, what steps can we take to preserve more jobs for Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the first three quarters of this year, compared to the same period last year, certainly the number is higher and will be higher for the whole of this year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM does not make any attempt to forecast.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But what we do is to track the number.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As the Member mentioned, based on the first three quarters of this year, it is higher than last year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the whole of this year, we believe it will be higher than the whole of last year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the last Sitting, the Minister for Trade and Industry had already stated his position that, if need be, when the time comes, we will provide support assistance either at the sectoral level or broad-based level.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For MOM and its tripartite partners, we accept that retrenchment will continue to happen because in Singapore, we have always believed in continuous restructuring.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In good times or in bad, retrenchment has always been there.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In fact, it is good for our economy and good for the workers as well, so that they can continue to, hopefully, take on better jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Having said so, we recognise that retrenchment will be a very difficult experience for our retrenched workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is the reason why the tripartite partners have put in place a special task force since early this year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As and when there is a retrenchment exercise, our task force will engage the employer, engage the workers and, together with the union, we will ensure that the retrenchment is carried out in a fair manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, if it is a unionised company, we will ensure that the union will negotiate for the retrenchment benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For companies that are not unionised, we will try to do mediation as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But more importantly is that having gone through the retrenchment exercise, we will collate information on the profile of the workers affected by retrenchment, in terms of their skills and education profile as well as their job preference.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In some cases, with the support of the employers and the union, we are even able to conduct career fairs onsite with the company for the retrenched workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In cases where they do not have a critical mass, we organise off-site job fairs for them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, the moment they are retrenched, we move in,  work with the companies to help the workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, I would say that, on the whole, let us support the retrenched workers the best that we can.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our main objective is to ensure that the retrenched workers will be able to go back to work as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are going to gather more employment information regarding workers – either self-employed or as part of the gig economy – because we believe that there will be implications for the workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Within the gig economy, the relationship between employer and employee has changed.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And what we are concerned about would be, if we see more workers becoming portfolio workers without the employer-employee relationship, then how would their welfare, their well-being, be taken care of, including skills upgrading, employability, retirement planning and so on?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Based on the survey findings, we will then decide on the next step.
